# Check catalogue

<!-- Generated by `preflight docs` from the check registry (ngs-preflight 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand; a test fails if this file is out of date. -->

This page lists every check in ngs-preflight 0.1.0. It is generated from the same registry the tool runs, so it cannot drift from the code. Run `preflight explain <ID>` to see one entry in the terminal.

## How to read this page

- **ERROR** means the submission is likely to fail or give wrong results. Fix it first.
- **WARN** means something looks wrong or risky. Review it; with `--strict` it counts as an error.
- **INFO** is a note or summary. It never affects the exit code.
- In the message text, anything in `{braces}` is filled in with values from your files when the check fires.
- Exit codes of `preflight check`: `0` pass, `1` errors found (or warnings with `--strict`), `2` warnings only, `3` tool or usage error.

## Target regions (BED)

<a id="bed001"></a>
### BED001: BED file can be read

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} Tools that read this file will stop, or silently skip those lines, so part of your target regions could be lost.

**How it works**

Each non-header line must have at least 3 columns separated by tabs, where columns 2 and 3 are integers. Lines starting with 'track', 'browser' or '#' are header lines: they are allowed and counted (see BED009). Blank lines are ignored. Gzip-compressed BED files are decompressed first.

**Suggested fix**

> Open the file and correct or remove the listed lines. Each line needs a chromosome name, a start and an end, separated by tabs, with start and end as whole numbers.

<a id="bed002"></a>
### BED002: Start and end make sense

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {have} impossible coordinates (for example line {line}: start {start:,}, end {end:,}). A region must start at 0 or later and end after it starts; empty or backwards regions are rejected by most tools or silently ignored.

**How it works**

Every interval must satisfy 0 <= start < end. BED is 0-based, half-open.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the start and end columns on the listed lines. If start and end were swapped, swap them back; empty regions (start equal to end) can be deleted.

<a id="bed003"></a>
### BED003: Chromosome names exist in the reference

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {summary} in the BED file cannot be found in the reference: {contigs}. {hint} Tools will fail or skip these regions, so the data you expect to be analysed would be missing.

**How it works**

Every contig name in column 1 is compared, exactly and case-sensitively, with the sequence names in the reference .fai/.dict. If adding or removing a 'chr' prefix (including MT <-> chrM) would make every missing name match, the message says so and points to 'preflight fix-bed'.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="bed004"></a>
### BED004: Intervals stay inside their chromosome

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {extend} past the end of {its} chromosome in the reference (for example line {line}: {contig} is {length:,} bp long but the interval ends at {end:,}). This usually means the BED was made for a different genome build, or has typing errors.

**How it works**

For contigs present in the reference, end must be <= the contig length from the .fai/.dict.

**Suggested fix**

> Confirm the BED was made for the same genome build as the reference (for example GRCh38, not GRCh37). If it was, correct or remove the listed lines.

<a id="bed005"></a>
### BED005: Intervals are sorted

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The BED file is not sorted: {reason}. Several common tools (bedtools, tabix, many variant callers) need sorted regions and will stop, or quietly give wrong answers, if they are not.

**How it works**

Sorted means every chromosome is one contiguous block, starts do not decrease inside a block, and the blocks follow either the reference order (when a reference is given) or plain alphabetical order (as produced by 'sort -k1,1 -k2,2n').

**Suggested fix**

> Run: preflight fix-bed --sort <file> --out <sorted file>. Add --reference to sort in reference order.

<a id="bed006"></a>
### BED006: No overlapping or touching intervals

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {what}. Counted as written, the targets add up to {raw}, but they cover only {merged} once overlaps are merged ({before} regions become {after}). Overlaps can double-count coverage and make some tools report the same region twice.

**How it works**

Intervals are sorted per chromosome. An interval that starts before the furthest end seen so far overlaps; one that starts exactly at that end is book-ended (touching). Merged territory is computed after joining both kinds, like 'bedtools merge'.

**Suggested fix**

> Run: preflight fix-bed --merge <file> --out <merged file>, or remove the duplicates by hand.

<a id="bed007"></a>
### BED007: Coordinates look 0-based (heuristic)

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> This BED file may use 1-based coordinates. This is a heuristic guess from patterns in the file, not a certainty: {reasons}. BED files are 0-based, so if the file really is 1-based, every region would be shifted by one base, which can drop or add a base at every edge.

**How it works**

Heuristic, and deliberately conservative. It looks for one kind of evidence: among neighbouring non-overlapping regions on a chromosome, at least 5 are separated by exactly 1 base, at least 3 times as many as touch directly, and they make up at least 10% of neighbour pairs. A start of 0 anywhere rules out 1-based and silences the check. Sparse target lists carry no such pattern, so most 1-based files cannot be detected.

**Suggested fix**

> Check how the file was produced. If the coordinates came from a spreadsheet, a 1-based 'closed interval' export or a VCF/GFF-style list, subtract 1 from the start column and leave the end column alone. If you are sure the file is 0-based BED, you can ignore this warning.

**Notes**

**Why a heuristic.** A BED file does not say which convention it uses, and a shifted file is still valid BED. The only evidence available is indirect, so this check looks for patterns that are rare in genuine 0-based files:

*Exactly-one-base gaps between neighbours.* Adjacent 0-based half-open regions that tile a stretch of genome share a boundary (the next start equals the previous end). The same regions written as 1-based closed intervals show a gap of exactly 1 between them. A gap of exactly 1 base is rare by chance (gaps between targets are usually tens to thousands of bases), so a file with many of them and few direct touches is suspicious.

*What is deliberately not used.* Coordinates written in the name column (for example `chr1:101-200` on a region with start 100) are not evidence either way: a correct 0-based file is often named with 1-based coordinates, and a careless one with its raw columns, so names cannot tell the two apart.

A `start` of 0 is impossible in a 1-based file, so any such interval silences the check. The thresholds are fixed in code (`ONE_BASED_MIN_EVIDENCE = 5` and the ratios above). The check has false negatives by design: sparse lists, such as a capture panel with well-separated exons, carry no pattern, and detecting those would need an annotation (exon starts from a known gene model), which ngs-preflight does not ship. It is meant to avoid false alarms, so it stays silent when unsure.

<a id="bed008"></a>
### BED008: Clean file formatting

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} {consequence}

**How it works**

Looks for a UTF-8 byte-order mark, CRLF (Windows) line endings, spaces used as column separators, and trailing spaces or tabs at the end of a line. The parser tolerates all four, so the other checks still run on the cleaned content.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="bed009"></a>
### BED009: Territory summary

**Severity:** INFO. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {summary}

**How it works**

Counts intervals, total and merged base pairs, the size distribution, intervals on alt/decoy/unplaced contigs (any name that is not chr1-22, X, Y or M, with or without 'chr'), presence of chrY and chrM, and the number of header lines that were ignored.

**Suggested fix**

> No action needed. Check that the totals match what you expect for your design (for example, the panel or exome you ordered).

<a id="bed010"></a>
### BED010: Interval sizes are plausible for a capture panel

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {what}. Very short regions are often typing mistakes (a start and end that are almost equal), and very long ones are usually whole genes or chromosomes pasted in by mistake; neither behaves like normal capture targets.

**How it works**

Flags intervals shorter than 20 bp and longer than 1,000,000 bp (1 Mb). Whole-genome or large-region designs can ignore this warning.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the listed lines. If they are intended (for example a large linkage region), you can ignore this warning; otherwise correct them.

<a id="bed011"></a>
### BED011: Interval names are unique

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {are} used for more than one interval (for example "{name}", {times} times). Results are often reported per name, so repeated names can be merged together or overwrite each other.

**How it works**

Only runs when column 4 (name) is present. Empty names and the placeholder '.' are ignored. Repeated names for different exons of one gene are common and may be fine.

**Suggested fix**

> Make the names unique (for example add an exon number), or ignore this warning if repeated names are intended.

## Sample sheet

<a id="ss001"></a>
### SS001: Required columns are present and filled in

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} The workflow cannot tell which samples and files to process without them.

**How it works**

The schema lives in src/ngs_preflight/schema/samplesheet.yaml. Required columns: sample_id, fastq_1 and, for FASTQ rows, fastq_2 (a row whose fastq_1 is a BAM or CRAM file needs no fastq_2, and the column may be absent). Optional: sex, family_id, paternal_id, maternal_id, library_id, lane. Column names must match exactly (case-sensitive); a close match such as 'Sample ID' is reported as a hint. Blank cells in required columns are also reported.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="ss002"></a>
### SS002: Sample IDs are unique

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} on more than one row without a different lane number (for example "{sample}" on lines {lines}). Two different samples with the same ID cannot be told apart, and their results would be merged or overwritten.

**How it works**

Rows may repeat a sample_id only when a 'lane' column exists and each repeated row has a distinct, non-blank lane (one sample sequenced on several lanes). Anything else is a duplicate.

**Suggested fix**

> Give every sample a unique ID. If one sample was sequenced on several lanes, add a lane column and give each row its own lane number.

<a id="ss003"></a>
### SS003: Sample IDs use safe characters

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not allowed (for example "{example}"). Sample IDs may only use letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, up to {max_length} characters. Spaces, slashes and other symbols break file names and many workflow tools.

**How it works**

Pattern from the schema: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$, maximum length 64. Blank IDs are reported by SS001, not here.

**Suggested fix**

> Rename the samples using only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore (_) and hyphen (-).

<a id="ss004"></a>
### SS004: Read files exist and are readable

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** the read-file folder (`--reads-dir`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} listed in the sample sheet could not be found or opened (for example "{path}" for sample "{sample}"{why}). The run would fail as soon as it tries to read them.

**How it works**

Relative paths are resolved against --reads-dir; absolute paths are used as written. Paths that are URLs (s3://, gs://, https://, ...) cannot be checked and are skipped. A file of 0 bytes counts as unreadable.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the file names for typos and that the files were copied to the folder given with --reads-dir. Upload any files that are missing.

<a id="ss005"></a>
### SS005: No file is listed twice

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} listed more than once (for example "{path}", used by {users}). Reads from one file would be counted under several samples, or the same reads used as both read 1 and read 2.

**How it works**

Paths are compared as written (after normalising slashes). A file appearing in two rows, or as both fastq_1 and fastq_2 of one row, is reported.

**Suggested fix**

> Check that each sample points at its own files. If you copied a row to make a new one, update its file names.

<a id="ss006"></a>
### SS006: Read 1 and read 2 files pair up

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not look like matching read 1 / read 2 pairs (for example sample "{sample}": {why}). Mispaired files make alignment fail or produce nonsense, often only after hours of compute.

**How it works**

File names are compared after replacing R1/R2 (or _1/_2) with a placeholder. When both files can be read (--reads-dir), the first 100 read names are compared (the first token of each header, ignoring a trailing /1 or /2). Files without an R1/R2 marker pass the name test.

**Suggested fix**

> Check that fastq_1 holds the read 1 file and fastq_2 the read 2 file from the same sequencing run, and that neither was renamed or swapped.

<a id="ss007"></a>
### SS007: Compressed files are intact

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** the read-file folder (`--reads-dir`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} damaged or incomplete (for example "{path}": {why}). A truncated download or interrupted copy is the usual cause, and it makes runs fail partway through.

**How it works**

Fast check, not a full validation. Every .gz/.bam: gzip signature, clean header, first 4 MiB decompresses. BGZF files (.bam, bgzip FASTQ): the 28-byte end-of-file marker must be present. Other gzip files up to 32 MiB: the whole stream is decompressed and its CRC verified. Larger non-BGZF gzip files cannot be proven complete cheaply, so only the head and trailer are checked.

**Suggested fix**

> Copy or download the file again, and compare its checksum (for example md5sum) with the one given by the sender.

<a id="ss008"></a>
### SS008: Sex values are from the allowed list

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not in the accepted list (for example "{value}" for sample "{sample}"). Downstream steps and the sex check need a recognised value.

**How it works**

Accepted values (case-insensitive): male/m/1, female/f/2, unknown/u/0/NA/n/a/'.'. A blank cell is allowed (sex unknown). The vocabulary is defined in src/ngs_preflight/schema/samplesheet.yaml.

**Suggested fix**

> Use one of: male, female, unknown (or M, F, U; or 1, 2, 0), or leave the cell blank.

<a id="ss009"></a>
### SS009: Family relationships are consistent

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} The family structure is used for relatedness checks and by family-aware analysis, so an inconsistent one can give wrong results.

**How it works**

Every non-empty paternal_id / maternal_id must be the sample_id of another row, and no sample may be its own father or mother. Blank, 0, '.', NA, n/a and none mean 'no parent recorded'.

**Suggested fix**

> Add a row for each parent (or clear the parent cell if the parent is not part of this submission), and make sure nobody is listed as their own parent.

## Reference compatibility

<a id="ref001"></a>
### REF001: Reference, BED and reads agree on naming and genome build

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} {consequence}

**How it works**

Naming style is read from the primary chromosomes (1-22, X, Y, M with or without 'chr'). A BAM header is compared with the reference; when there is no reference, the BED is compared with the BAM header instead (the BED-versus-reference case is reported in detail by BED003). Genome build is compared by contig length: the same chromosome with a different length means a different build (for example GRCh37 chr1 is 249,250,621 bp, GRCh38 chr1 is 248,956,422 bp). With --expected-build, the reference itself is also recognised by its lengths and compared with the expected build. Only BAM headers are read; see REF003.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="ref002"></a>
### REF002: Reads and reference list the same chromosomes

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} Some tools stop on this mismatch (for example with a sequence dictionary error), and any reads on the missing chromosomes would be ignored.

**How it works**

Compares the chromosome names in a BAM header with the reference. Reports names in the BAM that the reference lacks, and primary chromosomes (1-22, X, Y, M) the reference has but the BAM header lacks. Not reported when the naming style differs (REF001 explains that case).

**Suggested fix**

> Align the reads to the same reference you are submitting, or supply the reference the reads were aligned to. For a deliberately partial BAM, make sure its header lists only the chromosomes it contains.

<a id="ref003"></a>
### REF003: Read-file header could not be inspected

**Severity:** INFO. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {reason} The reference compatibility checks (REF001, REF002) did not cover this file.

**How it works**

BAM headers are read directly. CRAM headers are not inspected by this version, and a BAM whose header cannot be parsed is reported here (integrity problems are reported by SS007).

**Suggested fix**

> No action needed. If compatibility matters, confirm this file's reference by other means.

## Sample identity (optional, uses somalier)

<a id="id001"></a>
### ID001: No two samples are the same person

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Samples "{a}" and "{b}" have almost identical genotypes (relatedness {relatedness:.2f}, where 1.0 means the same person). Two different sample IDs should not hold the same individual: this is either a duplicate submitted under two names, or a sample swap.

**How it works**

somalier relate compares genotypes at about 17,000 common sites. Any pair of different sample IDs with relatedness above 0.9 is reported. Identical twins and the same person sequenced twice cannot be told apart by this test.

**Suggested fix**

> Check with the submitter which sample each file really belongs to. If one is a repeat of the other, give them the same sample ID and a different library or lane, or drop one.

<a id="id002"></a>
### ID002: Declared parent and child are related as expected

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The sample sheet says "{parent}" is the {role} of "{child}", but their genomes are only {relatedness:.2f} related (a parent and child should be about 0.50). Either the family tree in the sheet is wrong, or a sample has been swapped or mislabelled.

**How it works**

For every declared parent-child pair with both samples present, relatedness from somalier relate must fall between 0.35 and 0.65 (expected 0.5). Father and son swapped in the sheet is still parent-child, but the other parent link then fails, which is how swaps are usually caught.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the paternal_id / maternal_id columns against the family you were told about. If the sheet is right, ask the lab to confirm the sample labels.

<a id="id003"></a>
### ID003: Unrelated samples are unrelated

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Samples "{a}" and "{b}" are not declared as relatives in the sample sheet, but their genomes are {relatedness:.2f} related (unrelated people are close to 0). They may be relatives that the sheet does not mention, or the sheet may be incomplete.

**How it works**

Pairs with relatedness between 0.2 and 0.9 are reported when the sheet gives no relationship between them. Samples in the same family_id, parent-child pairs and siblings (sharing a declared parent) are never reported. Samples that are not in the sheet are not reported.

**Suggested fix**

> If these people are related, add the family_id and parent columns. If they should not be related, ask the lab whether samples were mixed up.

<a id="id004"></a>
### ID004: Declared sex matches the data

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The sample sheet says "{sample}" is {declared}, but the data look {inferred} (X-chromosome heterozygosity and X/Y read depth). Either the sex in the sheet is wrong or the sample has been mixed up.

**How it works**

somalier infers sex per sample from heterozygous calls on chrX and relative depth on chrX and chrY. Reported when the sheet says male or female and somalier infers the opposite. Samples declared unknown, or where somalier cannot decide, are not reported. Needs enough chrX/chrY sites; with very low coverage the call may be absent.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the sex entered for this sample. If the sheet is right, ask the lab to confirm the sample was not swapped.

<a id="id005"></a>
### ID005: Enough informative sites for an identity call

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Only {sites:,} of the identity sites could be read in "{sample}" ({low} is the minimum we consider reliable). With so few, the relatedness and sex results for this sample may be wrong, so treat the identity checks on it as unconfirmed.

**How it works**

Informative sites are those somalier genotyped as homozygous reference, heterozygous or homozygous alternate. Fewer than 5,000 (about 28% of the 17,766 sites in the standard hg38 list) triggers this warning. Typical causes: low coverage, a targeted panel that does not cover the sites, or a VCF without hom-ref records.

**Suggested fix**

> Use deeper data or a whole-genome/exome file for the identity check. For targeted panels, consider whether the identity check is meaningful at all.
